hints.title: Reverse Euclid Moves
hints.text: Moving forward allows doubling a coordinate or subtracting one from another. In reverse, this resembles the Euclidean algorithm.

hints.title: Greatest Common Divisor Power of Two
hints.text: Subtracting coordinates preserves gcd(x, y), while doubling a coordinate can only introduce factors of 2 into the gcd.

hints.title: GCD Reduction Condition
hints.text: Starting from (1, 1) where gcd is 1, any reachable point must have gcd(targetX, targetY) equal to a power of 2.

hints.title: Power of Two GCD Test Implementation

complexity.notes: Euclidean GCD computation followed by factoring powers of 2.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating grid searches or reachability graphs causes combinatorial explosion.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies that subtract/double transitions preserve all odd prime factors of gcd(X, Y).
